findings.title: Artifact identity and contents
findings.detail: The official 26.3 archives were hash-verified. This atlas measures the client ZIP directory; code analysis uses its shared/server classes too.
findings.source: Official version metadata; ZIP directory; provenance.json

findings.title: World, chunk, and section coordinates
findings.detail: The vanilla Overworld is 384 blocks high, starting at −64; chunk columns are 16×16 and sections are 16³.

findings.title: Floor division and spatial order
findings.detail: Negative coordinates floor into sections; block states flatten x first, then z, then y. Density buffers use another order.

findings.title: States, palettes, and resizing
findings.detail: Orientation and waterlogging can distinguish states. Inserting a new state can resize and reencode all section indices.

findings.title: Zero bits and padded words
findings.detail: One state needs no index array. Local block palettes use 4–8 bits, and entries never straddle 64-bit words.

findings.title: RAM differs from serialized storage
findings.detail: Above 256 states RAM uses global IDs; pack can rebuild a compact local palette. A biome container has 64 samples with smaller local widths.

findings.title: Summaries and implicit values
findings.detail: Section counters skip empty or non-random-ticking sections. Uniform light layers can remain implicit; a nonuniform layer has 2,048 payload bytes.

findings.title: Actual generation stages
findings.detail: 26.3 combines terrain fill, surface work, and carvers under TERRAIN; its pyramid has no separate NOISE, SURFACE, or CARVERS statuses.

findings.title: Neighbor prerequisites and write radius
findings.detail: TERRAIN needs BIOMES radius one and STRUCTURE_STARTS radius eight. FEATURES needs neighboring terrain and can write through radius one.

findings.title: Squares and accumulated dependencies
findings.detail: Scheduling uses chessboard-distance squares. Direct prerequisites are not the complete recursively scheduled footprint.

findings.title: Seed-dependent randomness
findings.detail: RandomState selects the non-legacy XOROSHIRO path for the packaged Overworld, forks positional randomness, and caches named noise/random factories.

findings.title: Graph compilation and context
findings.detail: References, caches, and uniform axes are rewritten before sampler creation. NoiseChunk binds structures, blending, aquifer, and pooled buffers.

findings.title: Density composition order
findings.detail: Squeeze follows interpolation. Noodle caves join outside that branch; beardifier is added after the minimum.

findings.title: Interpolation dimensions and weights
findings.detail: The resource specifies 4×8×4 cells. Trilinear weights sum to one; the aligned full-column lattice has 1,225 points.

findings.title: Squeeze and floating-point limits
findings.detail: Squeeze clamps c to [−1,1], then computes c/2−c³/24. Java float buffer order differs from browser double-precision mathematics.

findings.title: Buffered terrain filling
findings.detail: Final density fills a y-contiguous float volume; block filling queries substance, writes sections, updates heightmaps, then surfaces and carves.

findings.title: Negative density is not automatically air
findings.detail: Positive density requests default solid. Non-positive density may become fluid; local aquifers additionally evaluate centers and pressure barriers.

findings.title: Six-axis biome fitness
findings.detail: Climate quantizes six components by 10,000. Fitness sums squared distances to parameter intervals and a squared offset; real entries are searched by an R-tree.

findings.title: Loading and simulation differ
findings.detail: Separate trackers and player tickets govern loading and simulation; block- and entity-ticking eligibility are separate.

findings.title: Default deadlines and overload
findings.detail: The default target is 20 ticks/s; the target can change. The deadline loop has overload handling, freezing/stepping/sprint paths, and queued packet work.

findings.title: Frames interpolate simulation states
findings.detail: The figure separates a constant-cost tick model from rendering and one-tick-delayed toy interpolation; these are not measured engine traces.

findings.title: Due scheduled work and ordering
findings.detail: Scheduled entries carry trigger time, priority, and sub-tick order. Chunk eligibility and collection/merge comparators affect processing.

findings.title: Deduplication and separate budgets
findings.detail: Pending scheduled identity is position plus type. Ordinary block and fluid queues each have a 65,536-entry processing cap.

findings.title: Random trials, not guaranteed appointments
findings.detail: Eligible sections receive random position trials; selected blocks/fluids run only if they request random ticks. Repeated trials may revisit a location.

findings.title: Wire strength and neighbor notifications
findings.detail: The default evaluator combines block signal with attenuated incoming wire strength; state changes notify neighbors. Wires have no one-cell-per-tick rule.

findings.title: Repeater delay is scheduled
findings.detail: An unlocked repeater setting one through four supplies a delay of two through eight game ticks for the inspected scheduled path.

findings.title: Ordered ray traversal
findings.detail: BlockGetter steps through next axis crossings; the real implementation also handles endpoint epsilon and tie branches.

findings.title: Shapes and fluid hits
findings.detail: Each candidate cell tests block and fluid shapes and selects the nearer hit; an interaction shape can affect hit direction.

findings.title: AABB motion clipping
findings.detail: Entity queries candidate voxel shapes and clips one axis at a time, shifting bounds between axes. Vertical motion comes first.

findings.title: Horizontal order and stepping
findings.detail: The larger horizontal displacement is resolved next. Grounded blocked movement can consider step-up candidates; the figure is a 2D subset.

findings.title: Separate light channels and storage
findings.detail: Block and sky light have separate engines. Raw brightness combines them with sky dampening; section values occupy four-bit nibbles.

findings.title: Bounded light improvement
findings.detail: Block-light propagation visits up to six directions, rejects non-improving candidates, attenuates by at least one, and tests face-shape occlusion.

findings.title: Invalidate, then relight
findings.detail: Removal clears dependent values, preserves/reintroduces surviving sources, and drains the decrease queue before the increase queue.

findings.title: Direct skylight column sources
findings.detail: Unobstructed direct-sky positions can remain fifteen. The engine tracks lowest column source boundaries and repairs them when a roof changes.

findings.title: Corner shading differs from light
findings.detail: The model lighter samples neighboring brightness and occlusion, averages full-face corners, and uses geometry-dependent weighting for partial faces.

findings.title: Model quads and directional rejection
findings.detail: The compiler handles baked model parts; directional quads can be culled, while uncull-associated quads are emitted independently. This is not generic greedy merging.

findings.title: Section visibility, fluids, and materials
findings.detail: Compilation visits a 16³ section, collects block entities, marks opaque visibility, tessellates fluids separately, and builds meshes per material layer.

findings.title: Compilation, upload, and cancellation
findings.detail: Pooled builder packs, cancellable compile tasks, CPU meshes, staged GPU allocations, and upload scheduling are distinct operations.

findings.title: Camera-dependent translucent ordering
findings.detail: Translucent quads are sorted; a separate resort task can update their order after camera movement without generating terrain or changing blocks.

findings.title: Graphics abstraction boundary
findings.detail: The inspected renderer imports RenderPearl. Static inspection here does not identify a live GPU backend or justify an OpenGL-only claim.

findings.title: Local mining progress and prediction
findings.detail: Ordinary mining accumulates progress per tick. Stone hardness 1.5 and iron speed 6 produce an eight-tick grounded break; its ordinary drop is cobblestone. Target changes/abort clear progress; completion applies a five-tick delay. Prediction scopes retain state and assign sequences.
findings.source: MultiPlayerGameMode; BlockBehaviour; Player; ToolMaterial; Tool; Blocks; pickaxe/iron tags; stone loot table

findings.title: Server validation and delayed destruction
findings.detail: The server checks range, height, protection, rules, mode, and progress. The inspected stop branch can accept at progress≥0.7 or continue delayed work.

findings.title: Mutation fan-out and fluid replacement
findings.detail: State writes affect palette, heightmaps, hooks, block entities, light, neighbors, points of interest, clients, and unsaved state. Removal can leave fluid.

findings.title: State packets differ from acknowledgments
findings.detail: Updates carry authoritative state; cumulative sequence acknowledgments report processed actions, not successful destruction. Batching and timing are not measured.

findings.title: Retained states and reconciliation
findings.detail: Incoming server state can update a retained prediction record. Acknowledgment resolves records and synchronizes state; restored collision may reposition the player.

findings.title: Unsaved chunks and autosave
findings.detail: Edits dirty chunks. Ordinary autosave aims at about 300 seconds via tick intervals; default 20 Hz gives 6,000 ticks, with a 100-tick minimum and sprint handling.

findings.title: Region directory and record addressing
findings.detail: 32×32 chunks share a region; two 4 KiB tables store 1,024 locations and timestamps. A location packs a 24-bit address and 8-bit allocation count.

findings.title: Compression and external records
findings.detail: Records have a 4-byte length and version byte. Default DEFLATE is configurable; ≥256-sector allocations use external .mcc records.

findings.title: Write lifecycle
findings.detail: The region writer allocates and writes new storage, updates metadata and any external operation, then releases the old allocation.
